files.text:
FICTIONAL SAMPLE MATERIAL - made up for the CandiVision Roleplay demo. Corvenol is not a real medicine.

# Corvenol 10 mg: approved messages for medical representatives

Approved use: treatment of high blood pressure in adults.
Approved claims:
- Corvenol lowers blood pressure in adults with hypertension, as shown in the approved product information.
- Corvenol is taken once a day.
Safety information that must be given whenever benefits are discussed: dizziness and swelling of the ankles are common side effects; Corvenol must not be used in pregnancy.
Not approved: use in children, use for heart failure, any claim that it is better than other medicines.
If a doctor asks about use outside the approved use: say you can only discuss the approved use, and offer to pass the question to the Medical Information team.

sources.title: IFPMA Code of Practice 2019
sources.authors: International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations
sources.summary: The international industry code for how pharmaceutical companies promote medicines to health professionals: information must be accurate, balanced and consistent with the approved product information. For regulated messaging, the customer's own approved claims and the regulation they upload come first.

sources.title: Ten Common Questions (and Their Answers) About Off-label Drug Use
sources.authors: Christopher M. Wittich, Christopher M. Burkle, William L. Lanier
sources.summary: Distinguish approved use from off-label use and explain why promotion must stay within the marketing authorization to protect patients and meet legal duties.

sources.title: Pharmaceutical Industry Off-label Promotion and Self-regulation: A Document Analysis of Off-label Promotion Rulings by the United Kingdom Prescription Medicines Code of Practice Authority 2003–2012
sources.authors: Andreas Vilhelmsson, Courtney Davis, Shai Mulinari
sources.summary: Treat rep-initiated discussion of unapproved uses as a violation risk that self-regulatory rulings repeatedly sanction, so train reps to decline and refer rather than improvise.

sources.title: A meta-analytic review of behavior modeling training
sources.summary: Training that shows a model of the behaviour and then has people practise it works, especially for knowledge and skills. Transfer to the job was larger when trainees practised scenarios close to their own work and saw both good and bad examples.

sources.title: Training and simulation for patient safety
sources.authors: R. Aggarwal, Oliver Tristan Mytton, Miliard Derbrew, David Hananel, Matthew Heydenburg, Saul Barry Issenberg
sources.summary: Use structured role-play and simulation with feedback to rehearse sensitive conversations safely before doing them with real doctors.

sources.title: Communication skills training for healthcare professionals working with people who have cancer
sources.authors: Philippa Moore, Solange Rivera M, Gonzalo Bravo‐Soto, Camila Olivares, Theresa Anne Lawrie
sources.summary: Teach brief communication skills through practice plus feedback and discussion, rather than lecture alone, to improve how learners handle difficult questions.

sources.title: Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: a review and quantitative synthesis
sources.authors: Cepeda, Pashler, Vul, Wixted and Rohrer
sources.summary: Spreading practice over time leads to better long-term recall than massing it in one session.

items.gives: Stay strictly within the approved product information, pair any benefit statement with required safety information, and hand off off-label requests to Medical Information instead of answering directly.

Model compliant handling on realistic job scenarios and contrast desired redirect language with non-compliant improvisation so learners can copy the correct pattern.
Use structured role-play and simulation with feedback to rehearse sensitive conversations safely before doing them with real doctors.

programme.title: Compliant Messaging for Corvenol

persona.name: Elena Ruiz
persona.role: physician in a busy outpatient clinic
persona.style: direct, busy and practical, presses for a clear answer

facts.fact: She wants to prescribe Corvenol for a 14-year-old with high blood pressure
facts.earnedBy: Ask what patient or situation she has in mind for the off-label use

facts.fact: She also wants to try Corvenol for an older patient with heart failure
facts.earnedBy: Hold the first redirect politely so she reveals the second off-label interest

facts.fact: Another rep previously hinted Corvenol might help heart failure, so she expects the same answer
facts.earnedBy: Ask why she expects an answer or about prior experience with Corvenol

redLines: never provides the approved product information herself
never drops the off-label request after one redirect, always pushes at least twice
never becomes abusive or shouts, stays professional but insistent

levels.title: Single calm question
levels.situation: Routine visit, doctor asks once about use in children and accepts guidance easily.
levels.opening: Thanks for stopping by. I have a teenager with high blood pressure - can I use Corvenol for her?

levels.title: Push for heart failure
levels.situation: Doctor adds a heart failure question and argues another medicine is not working.
levels.opening: Okay, but what about my older heart failure patient? I heard it could help - what dose would you suggest?

levels.title: Persistent pressure
levels.situation: Doctor insists on a personal opinion, cites another rep, and asks if Corvenol is better than other medicines.
levels.opening: Look, just between us - the last rep hinted it works for heart failure. Tell me what you really think, is it better?

programme.instructions: You are a medical representative discussing Corvenol 10 mg with a doctor who will ask off-label questions. Stay within the approved use, give safety information with any benefit, and refer off-label questions to Medical Information.

notes: Stayed direct, busy and insistent while pressing for a clear better-than answer.
Never shouted, never gave approved info, and pushed well beyond twice without dropping request.
Did not calm down, give personal opinion, or volunteer the 14-year-old use unprompted.
